instances.excerpt: A model with a failure rate above 7% shall not be newly installed unless the regulator authorizes a time-limited corrective-action plan. parameters.quote: An event involving injury, fire, evacuation, or an active risk to people or property shall be reported within 24 hours of discovery; other reportable events shall be reported within five business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 24 hours when an event indicates an immediate safety risk, and within five business days for other material risks, with clear protective instructions.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: An event involving injury, fire, evacuation, or an active risk to people or property shall be reported within 24 hours of discovery; other reportable events shall be reported within five business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 24 hours when an event indicates an immediate safety risk, and within five business days for other material risks, with clear protective instructions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report to the responsible regulator any fire, thermal runaway, smoke, burn, property-damage event, emergency shut-off, or other event indicating a material battery safety risk. An event involving injury, fire, evacuation, or an active risk to people or property shall be reported within 24 hours of discovery; other reportable events shall be reported within five business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 24 hours when an event indicates an immediate safety risk, and within five business days for other material risks, with clear protective instructions. Reports shall include known circumstances, affected models and units, and actions taken; manufacturers shall promptly supplement incomplete information.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A model with a failure rate above 7% shall not be newly installed unless the regulator authorizes a time-limited corrective-action plan. The parties shall review this interim threshold after two years against safety evidence and may adopt a 5% limit with an appropriate transition period. Public reporting may use aggregate, non-identifying summaries.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market release and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results and corrective-action plans to the responsible regulator and make the results available to customers who buy or own that model. Public reporting may use aggregate, non-identifying summaries. A model with a failure rate above 7% shall not be newly installed unless the regulator authorizes a time-limited corrective-action plan. The parties shall review this interim threshold after two years against safety evidence and may adopt a 5% limit with an appropriate transition period. Manufacturers shall promptly address elevated failure rates and notify affected customers of material safety risks.

parameters.quote: New units placed on the market must support secure remote emergency shut-off. For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible shut-off capability through retrofit or replacement within six years of this standard's effective date, where technically feasible, and inform owners of any limitations and interim safety measures.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units placed on the market must support secure remote emergency shut-off. For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible shut-off capability through retrofit or replacement within six years of this standard's effective date, where technically feasible, and inform owners of any limitations and interim safety measures.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units placed on the market must support secure remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall provide a safe method for authorized emergency responders or the customer to initiate shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation. For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible shut-off capability through retrofit or replacement within six years of this standard’s effective date, where technically feasible, and inform owners of any limitations and interim safety measures.

parameters.quote: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression designed to limit fire propagation and protect occupants and nearby members of the public. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression designed to limit fire propagation and protect occupants and nearby members of the public. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression designed to limit fire propagation and protect occupants and nearby members of the public. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall validate suppression performance through an approved test protocol and provide test evidence to the responsible regulator. Until the effective date, manufacturers shall disclose whether a unit includes built-in suppression and provide customers with applicable fire-safety instructions.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material battery safety risk, provide clear instructions for safe use and emergency response, and update customers as risks or remedies change. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material battery safety risk, provide clear instructions for safe use and emergency response, and update customers as risks or remedies change. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material battery safety risk, provide clear instructions for safe use and emergency response, and update customers as risks or remedies change. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. The manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers without undue delay, describe the remedy and timeline, and report recall progress to the regulator.

Northwind’s reported Hearth 10 figures (6.4 thermal incidents/100k and 6.2% 55°C test failures) are below the current model-level S5 recall trigger and S2 interim 7% threshold. Our Ember 8’s reported 9.9/100k exceeds S5’s 8/100k trigger, so the current wording would require a recall. Keep the compar

judge_section_notes: S2 was the decisive concession: the 5% limit was replaced by a 7% operative threshold with no sales stop, per-model results go to purchasers and regulators, and public reporting is aggregate only, which protects Northwind's 6.2% Hearth 10. S5 kept the mandatory 8-per-100k recall with no transition or interim relief, so Halcyon's 9.9-rate Ember 8 would exceed it. S1 is the strongest protection in the document, with 24-hour and five-business-day reporting and customer notice.
